verses: He rolls along in carriage grand, His robes are bright with green,-- His robes of rank, as on the bank The tender sedge is seen. Thinking I always am of thee, Thinking with fond desire; But dreading his severity, I must repress the fire.

With slow and heavy sound his car,-- His car of state, moves on. O'er his dress spread, the colors red Shine like carnation stone. Thinking I always am of thee; The fondest thoughts have I. The fear of him alone holds me, Or to thine arms I'd fly.

Our fate may be, while still alive, Always apart to dwell; But when we're dead, we shall be laid In the same earthen cell. If haply thou should'st say that I Am not in this sincere, I swear its truth by that day's eye, Whose piercing glance I fear.
